 ORDER 1.

This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is filed by accused Nos.1 to 3 with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in C.C.No.18767/2016 pending before the Court of VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, arising out of Crime No.157/2014 registered by Amruthahally Police Station, Bengaluru City, for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 471 read with Section 34 of IPC.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for respondent No.2 submit that the dispute between the NC: 2024:KHC:10289 parties has been amicably settled and the petitioners have filed I.A.No.1/2024 under Section 482 read with Section 320 of Cr.P.C. with a prayer to permit B M Vijaykumar vs State Of Karnataka By on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183197117/

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 has also filed a separate affidavit stating that the dispute between the parties has been amicably settled.
They jointly submit that the settlement arrived at between the parties is voluntary without there being any undue influence or coercion.
4. Parties, who are present before the Court are identified by their respective Advocates.
Application I.A.No.1/2024 filed by the petitioners with a prayer to permit them to compound the offence is supported by affidavit of the parties.

In paragraph No.3 of the Affidavit filed by the petitioners, it has been averred as follows:-
"3. We Deponents in the above matter have come forward to settle the criminal proceedings initiated by Respondent No.2 upon deliberation with Respondent No2,
as Respondent No.2 while initiating the subject criminal matter was under mental distress and in consideration of the future prospects of NC: 2024:KHC:10289 both the families.
And, we are desirous of setting the matter considering that the dispute is civil in nature.

Hence, we have agreed to compound criminal case in C.C.No.18767/2016 for offences punishable under section 419, 420, 471 r/w 34 of IPC pending before the Learned Addl Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore with Respondent No.2."
5.

Taking into consideration that the dispute between the parties has been settled amicably and the dispute is private in nature and also considering the fact that the offences alleged are compoundable, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioners in I.A.No.1/2024 is required to be granted.

Accordingly, the following order:-
6. I.A.No.1/2024 is allowed.
Parties are permitted to compound the offences for which the petitioners have been charge sheeted.
Consequently, petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings in C.C.No.18767/2016 pending before the Court of VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bengaluru, arising out of Crime No.157/2014 registered by Amruthahally Police NC:
2024:KHC:10289 Station, Bengaluru City, for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 471 read with Section 34 of IPC is quashed.
